trust.register_intro: Every AI pick recorded before the match: time of publication, the odds after publication, the odds just before kick-off and the result. Losses sit next to wins — nothing is removed and nothing is corrected after the fact.
trust.sum_clv_hint: {n} picks with morning and closing odds · 95% interval: {low} to {high}
trust.sum_beat_hint: odds shortened after publication · unchanged {same} · drifted {worse}
trust.sum_roi_hint: flat stake, {n} picks, average odds {odds} · after the 12% Polish tax: {taxed}
trust.verdict_too_few: Too few picks to judge an edge: we need at least {min} with CLV, there are {n}.
trust.verdict_behind: The market regularly moves against our picks (on average {clv}). On these numbers we have no edge.
trust.verdict_level: Average CLV of {clv} is indistinguishable from zero — on these numbers there is no visible edge over the market.
trust.verdict_small: After publication the market moves towards the pick more often than against it, but only by {clv} on average — less than the market margin and the 12% tax. A signal, not a profit.
trust.verdict_ahead: After publication the market regularly moves towards our picks (on average {clv}). Evidence of an edge, not a promise of profit — a single match stays a lottery.
trust.clv_why_title: Why is CLV the best evidence?
trust.clv_why_1: The closing price — 10–30 minutes before kick-off — is the best-informed price there is: the market already knows the line-ups, the injuries and the decisions of thousands of players.
trust.clv_why_2: If the odds regularly shorten after our pick, the market reaches our view only later. That cannot be luck: a lucky run of hits can last for months, while an edge in CLV has to hold over hundreds of matches.
trust.clv_why_3: A hit rate is easy to inflate by picking only favourites. CLV does not allow that — it measures whether we knew something before the market, not whether the event was likely.
trust.clv_why_formula: CLV = morning odds ÷ closing odds − 1. Example: a pick at 1.50 that closes at 1.40 → +7.1%.
trust.rule_before: Only picks recorded before kick-off are included. Rejected for being recorded after the start: {count} of {checked}.
trust.rule_once: A pick is recorded once: the market, the selection and the chance do not change afterwards. The publication time is the server’s record time, shown next to every pick.
trust.rule_live: Live picks ({count}) are made during the match, so they are not in the register.
trust.rule_ref: Morning odds are the bookmaker median from the first odds snapshot after publication — usually 9:00 on match day. A pick recorded later is compared with the odds at publication, never with odds from before it.
trust.rule_close: Closing odds are the median from the last snapshot, 10–30 minutes before kick-off.
trust.rule_missing: A pick without odds (a market our source does not price, or a gap in the snapshots) counts towards hits, but not towards CLV and return. In this selection {share} of started picks have CLV.
trust.rule_scope: These are the same picks as on the Accuracy tab (pick of the day, model badges, analyses, reports), including leagues on probation. A repeat of the same selection counts once — the first record.
trust.leagues_more: Most picks in the selected period and market.
trust.locked: Recorded {time}, {lead} before kick-off. The selection is revealed at kick-off.
trust.upcoming_note: {count, plural, one {# pick is} other {# picks are}} waiting for the match — the record time is visible, the selection is revealed at kick-off.
trust.error: Could not load the register. Try refreshing the page.
trust.disclaimer: 18+. The register is a statistic, not advice or an encouragement to gamble. Odds are the median of several bookmakers, with no links — the site does not take bets. Past results do not tell you what happens tomorrow. Play responsibly — gambling can be addictive.

growth.posts_bio_title: Link for the bio (links in captions are not clickable)
growth.posts_rules: Every link carries utm (source = channel, utm_medium=social, campaign = post type) — accounts from it show up in “Sign-up sources”. Nothing is published automatically. Informational content: no encouragement to gamble, no bookmaker names, misses next to hits, always 18+.
growth.posts_coupon_lead: The free coupon of the day with odds (bookmaker median, no names) and the model’s chance.
growth.posts_coupon_none: No coupon to publish right now — the coupon of the day is built at 9:30 and the post disappears once its first match kicks off.
growth.posts_recap_lead: All of yesterday’s settled model picks, the pick of the day and the coupon of the day — misses named.
growth.posts_recap_none: Nothing was settled yesterday — settlement runs overnight, check in the morning.
growth.posts_week_lead: The last 7 full days: hits and what the model promised, pick of the day, coupon of the day.
growth.posts_week_none: Nothing was settled in the last 7 days.

lineups.title: Line-ups
lineups.stage_expected_hint: The provider usually publishes starting XIs 20–60 minutes before kick-off. Until then we count absentees from the injury and suspension list.
lineups.regular_legend: Regular = in the starting XI in at least 6 of the last 10 matches.
lineups.unknown_regulars: Too few known line-ups to tell the regulars.
lineups.conclusion_some: {team}: {missing} of {core} regulars missing — normal rotation, no veto.
lineups.conclusion_unknown: {team}: too few known line-ups to judge.
lineups.note: The numerical model does not use line-ups. A pick on a team with a weakened line-up (3+ regulars, the first-choice keeper or the top scorer missing) is left out of coupons and the pick of the day.
lineups.warning_hint: Weakened line-up of the team this pick backs — several regulars, the first-choice keeper or the top scorer missing.
lineups.leg_warning_after: Published before line-ups — the pick stays unchanged.
